label: sec:co2-computation-intro
html: With heteronuclear bonding in place, add a third atom. Carbon dioxide CO_2 as a molecular braid couples a central carbon to two oxygens, each via a shared electron pair on the molecular Hecke strands. The LP dual selects linear O{=}C{=}O geometry. The optimum places the two C{=}O trefoils on opposite sides of the central strand. This configuration gives the VSEPR molecular geometry from \Phi_1 minimisation. The linear triatomic case isolates molecular geometry as a consequence of \Phi_1 minimisation, independent of bond order.
